rulings.challenge_claim: The row dismisses an internal seam at 28:7 on the ground that no speaker, addressee or formula marks the turn, but 28:7 opens verse-initially with a contrastive particle plus a hear-this-word imperative and an explicit second-person addressee, and neither 28:7 nor 28:8 is quoted anywhere in the row.
rulings.grounds: The bytes are exactly as challenged: oshb:Jer.28.7 opens אַךְ שְׁמַֽע נָא֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה and continues אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י דֹּבֵ֣ר בְּאָזְנֶ֑יךָ (byte tier) - a verse-initial contrastive particle, a second-person-singular hear-now imperative with a demonstrative object, and an explicit second-person addressee marking, standing at the turn the rejection weighs; the rationale names a contrastive hinge with no form and no verse, and of the five verses in the span the pointed splices cover 28:5, 28:6 and 28:9 only, so the two verses carrying the rejected rival are the two left unquoted. To that extent the absence word 'formula' over-reaches and the defect is real. The challenge's inference does not stand. The shape at 28:7 is the second-person-singular appeal form (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier - 28:7, 28:15, 37:20, 38:20), whose two sites outside this chapter fall inside the courtly address to the king, and its object here is the speaker's own word, not the word of YHWH; the summons form that the ruled internal-seam classes name as a discourse-frame imperative is the plural word-of-YHWH shape (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier), which the span does not carry. The claim that one device is read two ways in one scene fails on bytes: the same second-person appeal shape stands at oshb:Jer.28.15 שְׁמַֽע נָ֣א חֲנַנְיָ֑ה (byte tier), and the seam there is carried by the narrative reply formula reopening after the intervening word event at 28:12, not by the imperative - so the device carries no seam at either site. The speaker and addressee arms of the rejection are byte-true: 28:6 already addresses Hananiah in the second person singular, and 28:6 itself carries the resumptive narrative speech formula וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא (oshb:Jer.28.6, byte), so the repeated speaker formula inside the span stands at 28:6 and not at the weighed turn. Tier-1 text signals throughout; the parashah, paseq and ketiv/qere layers are empty at every MT key from 28:4 through 28:9, matching the disclosed silence.
rulings.remedy: In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the blanket absence with the named shape: state that 28:7 opens on a contrastive particle and a second-person-singular hear-now imperative whose object is the speaker's own word, then give the holding ground - no speaker or addressee change from 28:6, and the imperative is not the plural word-of-YHWH summons form that the internal-seam classes name. In boundary_rationale, splice the pointed 28:7 hinge at the site where it is argued instead of describing it. Test the cure must pass: a byte read of oshb:Jer.28.7 and oshb:Jer.28.8 must contradict no absence word left in the sentence - the test that killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: First item: the rejected-alternative sentence identifies neighbouring material by narrative position twice instead of by verse. Second item: the rationale calls the formula at 28:11 the full divine formula carried again, where the bytes give the bare two-word shape, and the English gloss departs from the paired Hebrew splice at both ends.
rulings.grounds: Both items stand and they are distinct defects in different fields. Register: strongest_rejected_alternative carries two position-only cross-references to neighbouring units inside one sentence, where cross-unit references are required to be verse-anchored; a position-only description cannot be checked against bytes on its own terms and stops naming the same material if the sequence changes. Formula object: oshb:Jer.28.11 reads כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (byte tier), the bare two-word shape, while oshb:Jer.28.2 reads כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (byte tier), the tsevaot-plus-Elohei-Yisrael stack. These are separate count objects - the koh-amar-headed full stack stands in 31 verses book-wide (sweep: 31 verses, skeleton tier), among them 28:2 and 28:14 but not 28:11 - so calling the 28:11 occurrence the full formula carried again imports the 28:2 form onto a verse that does not carry it, and the row's own signal key names the bare shape, leaving key and prose in disagreement about one site. Gloss parity: the pointed run spliced there runs from the formula through the king's name, while the English paired with it drops the formula's own rendering at the front and runs past the splice to the two-year clause at the back (web:Jer.28.11); each quoted English string is verbatim against the staged text, so the defect is extent, not fidelity. What verifies and must not be disturbed by the cure: the mouth is named as Hananiah's and is byte-true at the verse-initial speech formula of 28:11; the vav-less defective royal-name form at 28:11 is the spelling the bytes carry; and the petuchah and the single paseq seg recorded at MT 28:11 both match the inventories under the types claimed.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace both position-only references with verse anchors (the formula at verse 2; the word event at verse 12), keeping the field to its one-sentence rule. boundary_rationale: name the 28:11 formula as the bare koh-amar shape, and where the earlier occurrence is invoked, name the tsevaot-plus-Elohei-Yisrael stack as the distinct object it is. Re-cut the 28:11 gloss so its extent equals the splice at both ends, or extend the splice to the clause the English covers. Tests: a register sweep of every field must return no positional cross-unit reference; the formula label must survive a byte read of oshb:Jer.28.11 set against oshb:Jer.28.2; and gloss extent must equal splice extent at the paired site - the tests that killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: The boundary stands, but the supporting notes call the second word-event site a closing device when its bytes make it a verse-initial onset, rank the pair above rivals never swept, go silent on a paseq seg inside the span that the neighbouring unit discloses, and assert the said-to-Hananiah recurrence with no tier.
rulings.grounds: All four arms verify on bytes and inventories; the severity is corrected upward from the challenge's reading because two of them are validator-class defects rather than wording. First, oshb:Jer.29.30 opens וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier) verse-initially and is followed by a fresh oracle at 29:31-32, so it opens a word event and closes nothing, while the same shape is read correctly as an opener at 28:12 in the same field. The pair digit itself is exact: the shape stands in 21 verses book-wide and in exactly 2 across chapters 27 through 29 (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier - 28:12 and 29:30). Second, ranking that pair as the strongest tier-1 signal available for any boundary across the three chapters is a superlative carried with no sweep of the rivals, and the bytes place classified onset shapes at two of the three chapter openings: oshb:Jer.27.1 opens בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת יְהוֹיָקִ֥ם and oshb:Jer.28.1 opens וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא בְּרֵאשִׁית֙ מַמְלֶ֨כֶת֙ (byte tier for each) - a verse-initial regnal-accession header, and a verse-initial date frame carrying the same accession phrase mid-verse. A ranking or exclusivity claim is never dampened by a tier label. Third, a paseq seg stands at MT 28:14, inside this span, undisclosed, while the unit covering 28:10-28:11 discloses exactly that object one verse earlier - a span-relevant disclosure asymmetry inside one cluster. Fourth, the said-to-Hananiah recurrence is asserted untiered: the opening runs of oshb:Jer.28.5 and oshb:Jer.28.15 re-collate against each other at accent_stripped tier, not at byte tier, and a recurrence carrying a boundary must name the tier at which it recurs. The boundary is untouched: the word-event onset at 28:12 is byte-exact and an inventory member.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace the closing-device description with the byte-true role - a verse-initial word-event onset at 29:30 opening the oracle of 29:31-32; either drop the strongest-signal ranking or carry it with a digit-bearing sweep that names the rival onset shapes standing at 27:1 and 28:1; and add the MT 28:14 paseq seg to the span's disclosure (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position claimed). strongest_rejected_alternative: label the 28:5 and 28:15 recurrence at accent_stripped tier. Tests: the span-relevant mark-disclosure sweep must return no undisclosed seg in any layer; every superlative left in the field must carry an adjacent digit naming the swept object; and the recurrence sentence must survive a re-collation of both runs - the test that killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: First item, shared: the device-notes setumah at 28:16 is not carried by the marked-verse inventory. Second item: the WEB quotation of that verse drops the mark closing the embedded divine speech. Third item: the recurrence the seam rests on is asserted with no tier, and the mouth at the formula is unnamed.
rulings.grounds: The mark claim fails both arms at once, which is what carries the severity: the single-witness parashah layer records exactly two segs in MT chapter 28, petuchah at 28:11 and petuchah at 28:17 (sweep: 2 marked verses in the chapter), nothing at MT 28:16, and no setumah anywhere in the chapter - so neither the site nor the type asserted exists in the witness cited. Framing the mark as texture rather than warrant does not lower the bar: a single-witness mark citation either matches the inventory at its cited MT key or it does not, and this one does not. The quotation defect is distinct and also stands: the staged verse closes the embedded divine speech with a right single quotation mark standing before the verse-final right double mark, while the reproduction opens that embedded speech with the left single mark and supplies no closing partner, so the quoted span does not reproduce the staged text it claims to match (web:Jer.28.16); the words themselves are verbatim, so the defect is pairing, not wording. The recurrence arm stands as it does in the commissioned-reply unit at 28:12-28:14: the opening runs of oshb:Jer.28.5 and oshb:Jer.28.15 re-collate against each other at accent_stripped tier and differ in the pointed bytes, and this row's seam rests on that recurrence with no tier named. One sub-arm does not stand: the mouth at the 28:16 formula is not left unnamed - the same field frames 28:15-28:16 as the prophet's public delivery of the word commissioned at 28:12, which names the frame owner in substance, and the row carries no koh-amar digit that would require one.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: delete the setumah claim at 28:16 and state the span's parashah facts as the inventory carries them - nothing at MT 28:16, petuchah at MT 28:17 one verse past the close - and name which layer each absence statement covers, since the front-seam verse MT 28:14 does carry a paseq seg. boundary_rationale: re-quote web:Jer.28.16 so that the embedded speech's opening and closing marks are both reproduced, or exclude the inner mark from the quoted span; and add the accent_stripped tier label to the said-to-Hananiah recurrence there and in strongest_rejected_alternative. Tests: every mark claim must validate against the inventory at its MT key under the type claimed; the WEB quotation must pass a verbatim comparison with balanced curly pairing; and the recurrence must carry the tier a re-collation actually returns - the tests that killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row rejects the internal seam at 29:10 on speaker-and-addressee grounds alone, leaving undisclosed a convergence at the 29:9/29:10 juncture - a verse-final closure formula, a fresh speech-formula onset, and the mark it cites without its direction - and it cites three formula sites under one undifferentiated label.
rulings.grounds: Two of the three arms stand; the framing that the mark is disclosed without direction does not. The juncture is as described: oshb:Jer.29.9 closes verse-finally on נְאֻם יְהוָֽה and oshb:Jer.29.10 opens כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier for each), so a closure formula does stand immediately before a fresh onset at exactly the seam the row rejects, while the stated ground answers only frame owner and addressee. The closure device is in fact undisclosed across the whole span, not only at that juncture: it stands four times over three verses of the span - verse-final at 29:9, once at 29:11, twice at 29:14 - and neither the prose nor the signal keys carry it, although the ruled granularity makes it the operative corroboration test. On that same ruled reading the convergence does not cut: the closure corroborates only where a fresh qualifying onset follows, and a koh-amar carrying no frame-owner change and no fresh addressee is not one - which is why this is a disclosure defect and not a boundary error, and both of those negative findings are byte-true as the row states them. The label arm stands: 29:4 and 29:8 carry the tsevaot-plus-Elohei-Yisrael stack, 29:4 reading כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (byte tier), while 29:10 carries the bare shape, two distinct count objects cited under one term with only the full-stack key declared. The mark-direction arm does not stand: the field places the petuchah at MT 29:7 and the setumah at MT 29:9 around the two internal turns, which locates the 29:9 seg at the juncture in question. Both marks and the ketiv/qere at MT 29:14 match the inventory under their claimed types, and no paseq seg falls in the span.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: disclose the closure formula inside the span with its ruled role - verse-final at 29:9, once at 29:11 and twice at 29:14 - as corroboration and never as driver. strongest_rejected_alternative: weigh the 29:9 closure and 29:10 onset convergence explicitly and give the holding ground (no frame-owner change, no fresh addressee, one sustained address to the audience named at 29:4). boundary_rationale and observed_substrate_signals: split the formula label so that the full-stack sites at 29:4 and 29:8 and the bare-shape site at 29:10 are named as distinct objects, and add the bare-shape signal key. Tests: the corrected rejection must survive a byte read of oshb:Jer.29.9 and oshb:Jer.29.10 - no ground that passes over a verse-final closure standing immediately before a fresh onset - and every formula digit must name the object swept.

rulings.challenge_claim: At the juncture the row declares undecided it discloses the mark at 29:15 without its direction while reading the same layer as closing at 29:20; a second formula object and a rival onset inside the span go unquoted; and two paseq segs in the span are undisclosed while the ketiv/qere in one of those verses is disclosed.
rulings.grounds: All four arms verify. Direction: the field says a setumah closes the span at oshb:Jer.29.20 but says only that a setumah sits in the opening verse oshb:Jer.29.15; under the closing reading applied one clause earlier, the 29:15 seg divides 29:15 from 29:16 and is weak single-witness corroboration for the very alternative the row declares unsettled. The weight stays tier-3 and never a driver - the defect is the asymmetric disclosure at the crux, not the weight. Second object: oshb:Jer.29.16 opens the bare shape, which the row does quote, while oshb:Jer.29.17 opens כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (byte tier), koh-amar with tsevaot and without the Elohei-Yisrael element - a distinct count object (sweep: 50 verses carry the tsevaot-headed shape, skeleton tier; 29:17 is a member and 29:16 is not) - and it is undisclosed. Rival onset: the span's own last verse opens וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier), the plural hear-the-word-of-YHWH summons with a vocative naming the exiles (sweep: 10 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), standing immediately after 29:19, which carries the closure formula twice and ends on it verse-finally; that puts a live tier-1 seam at 29:19/29:20 which the row never weighs, while it does weigh 29:20/29:21. Marks: paseq segs stand at MT 29:16 and MT 29:18 inside the span, both undisclosed, while the ketiv/qere at MT 29:18 is disclosed - a one-layer omission inside a verse the row already cites. The parashah marks at MT 29:15 and MT 29:20 match the inventory under their claimed types, and all four English quotations in the field are verbatim against the staged text.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: state the 29:15 seg with the same closing direction used at 29:20, adding that under that reading it corroborates - weakly, single-witness - joining 29:15 to what precedes; and add the paseq segs at MT 29:16 and MT 29:18 (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position claimed). boundary_rationale: quote the tsevaot-headed formula at 29:17 and name it as its own count object. strongest_rejected_alternative: weigh the 29:19/29:20 juncture, naming the summons shape at 29:20 and the doubled verse-final closure at 29:19. PROPOSAL only, requiring explicit adoption and never author work: close this unit at 29:19 and open the next at 29:20 - the same seam raised independently against the unit that begins at 29:21. Tests: the span's mark-disclosure sweep must return no undisclosed seg in any layer; every formula cited must name its own count object; and the corrected rejection must survive a byte read of oshb:Jer.29.19 and oshb:Jer.29.20.

rulings.challenge_claim: First item: the discourse-imperative summons one verse before the front seam is a stronger, undisclosed rival for this unit's opening. Second item: the koh-amar the seam rests on is never quoted in the original language, its mouth and written medium are unnamed, a single-site name-form change inside the span is undisclosed, and a paseq seg in the span is undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The two items are distinct and both stand. Rival onset: oshb:Jer.29.20 opens וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier), the plural hear-the-word-of-YHWH summons with a vocative naming the exiles - a recurring book-wide shape (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier) standing immediately after a doubled verse-final closure formula at 29:19 and followed at once by the oracle this unit carries - while the disclosed alternative weighs only whether the curse formula of verse 22 should split from verse 21, and never whether that summons belongs forward as this unit's opening. The comparison to the summons cited from elsewhere in the book holds as a class parallel and not as a byte recurrence: the two needles differ at skeleton tier. Evidence mechanics: oshb:Jer.29.21 opens כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (byte tier) verse-initially, and the row's own pointed run begins after it at אֶל אַחְאָ֤ב בֶּן קֽוֹלָיָה֙, so the device carrying the seam is quoted in the other witness alone, against the standing requirement that a boundary-relevant original-language claim be spliced with its tier named. Ownership and medium are unnamed in the one stretch where formulas stand inside a quoted letter and, one chapter earlier, in a false prophet's mouth; the field's signal keys carry the speech formula alone with no letter-frame key, although the units at 29:4-29:14 and at 29:24-29:29 both declare that frame for the same document. The name-form change is byte-real and load-bearing on the row's own rejection: the fuller spelling אַחְאָ֤ב stands at 29:21 and the shorter base וּכְאֶחָ֔ב one verse later at 29:22 (byte tier; skeleton sweeps, finals-normalized: 1 verse each, book-wide), so the sentence binding verse 22 back to verse 21 by name rests on two different attested spellings without saying so. One paseq seg stands at MT 29:21 inside the span, undisclosed, while both parashah marks and the ketiv/qere and exegesis note at MT 29:23 are disclosed. What verifies: the resh-family royal spelling at 29:21 and its contrast with the nun-family forms at 29:1 and 29:3 are byte-true, and both setumah citations match the inventory under their types.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice the pointed formula at 29:21 with its tier at the site where the seam is argued; name whose mouth carries it and the written medium it stands inside; and disclose both attested spellings of the name at 29:21 and 29:22 with a per-spelling digit, since the rejection turns on the two names. observed_substrate_signals: add the letter-frame key already carried by the units at 29:4-29:14 and 29:24-29:29. device_notes: add the MT 29:21 paseq seg (single-witness, count-only). strongest_rejected_alternative: weigh the summons at 29:20 as the rival onset. PROPOSAL only, requiring explicit adoption and never author work: open this unit at 29:20 rather than 29:21 - the same seam raised independently against the unit that ends at 29:20. Tests: every boundary-carrying device must be spliced at byte tier at the verse where it is argued; the name claim must survive a per-spelling sweep with its digit; and the span's mark-disclosure sweep must return no undisclosed seg.

rulings.challenge_claim: The full title-stack formula standing verse-initially inside this span is neither quoted nor declared, so the unit is classed from the embedded quoted letter rather than from the divine formula that owns it; the medium is flattened from the plural the bytes carry to a single document; and the conjunctive form opening the span's first verse sits undisclosed on the row's own front seam.
rulings.grounds: All three arms verify, and a fourth defect of the same family stands beside them. Governing formula: oshb:Jer.29.25 opens כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (byte tier) verse-initially, inside the span, a member of the koh-amar-headed full-stack object (sweep: 31 verses book-wide, skeleton tier; inside chapters 27 through 29 it stands at 27:4, 27:21, 28:2, 28:14, 29:4, 29:8, 29:21 and 29:25), and it governs the quoted rival material at 29:26-29:28; the field carries no speech-formula signal at all and never quotes the formula, so ownership runs divine formula over embedded letter and the one question this stretch turns on is left unanswered. Medium: 29:25 charges the sending of סְפָרִ֗ים, a plural, while 29:29 reports הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה (byte tier for each), one document, and the account uses a single letter throughout - a precision defect rather than a structural one. Front seam: 29:24 opens וְאֶל (byte tier), a conjunctive form binding this address to the one just closed and standing exactly on this unit's own front seam, undisclosed, while the English paired with it carries no conjunction at all - a byte-true continuity signal that argues against the cut unless disclosed. Standing beside the challenge: the pointed run given at 29:27 is two words while the English paired with it is the whole verse (web:Jer.29.27), so gloss extent exceeds splice extent at that site. What verifies: the setumah at MT 29:23 and the petuchah at MT 29:29 match the inventory under their types; no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span; the defective gentilic at 29:27 is the spelling the bytes carry; and all three English quotations are verbatim against the staged text.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice the pointed formula at 29:25 with its tier, name it as the divine formula governing the quoted letter at 29:26-29:28, and add the matching speech-formula key to observed_substrate_signals. Correct the medium to the plural the bytes carry at 29:25, keeping the singular only where 29:29 warrants it. Disclose the conjunctive opening at 29:24 on the front seam and state why it does not carry continuity against the cut. Re-cut the 29:27 pairing so that gloss extent equals splice extent. Tests: every span-internal tier-1 formula must be quoted at byte tier and keyed; the cross-seam device at the front seam must be disclosed; and gloss extent must equal splice extent at every paired site - the test that killed the original.
